title: The Houthi Advance Is About More Than Just Iran
gist: The Houthis' Sept. 8 offensive seized Mokha, most of Yemen's Red Sea coast and key islands, giving them control over the Bab el-Mandeb just as Saudi Arabia was rerouting oil via its East-West pipeline to avoid Iranian control of Hormuz. Lynch argues this, and Algeria's rupture with the UAE, reflect a three-way regional contest (Iran axis, Saudi-led bloc, UAE-Israel Abraham Accords camp) spilling into Africa, not just Iranian strategy.

insights.claim: The Houthis' seizure of Mokha, most of Yemen's Red Sea coastline and several Red Sea islands lets them disrupt and deny shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint connecting Asia to the West via the Suez Canal.
insights.speaker: Marc Lynch
insights.so_what: Expect elevated shipping insurance, freight rates and rerouting around the Cape; bullish tanker/container rates, negative for Suez-dependent trade.

insights.so_what: Both Gulf oil exit routes are compromised, a major upside risk to crude prices and a supply shock for Saudi exports.
